Return raw JSON only. Do not use Markdown fences, introductory or concluding prose, comments, or any text outside the JSON. Do not invent enum values. Return exactly one row for every requested monitor, with no omitted or duplicated monitor IDs. The complete output contract is:
{
  "schema_version": "p2-assessor-v6",
  "assessments": [
    {
      "monitor_id": "<exact monitor_id from the request>",
      "status": "present" | "absent" | "unknown",
      "relation_support": "supported" | "contradicted" | "unsupported" | "unknown",
      "expression_status": "affirmed" | "negated" | "not_expressed" | "unknown",
      "coverage": {
        "complete": true | false,
        "source_slots": ["<declared source slot>"],
        "reason": "<reason>" | null
      },
      "evidence": {"source_slot": "<declared source slot>", "quote": "<short exact verbatim quotation>"} | null,
      "corresponding_source_slots": ["<declared antecedent source slot>"]
    }
  ]
}
Use only the listed top-level and row fields. The schema_version must be exactly p2-assessor-v6. For status=present, coverage must name covered declared source slots and evidence must contain a non-empty exact quotation from its source_slot. Status=present means the proposition is addressed by the available required sources; it does not by itself mean the proposition is affirmed. For status=present, coverage.complete must be true and source_slots must include every available required source slot; an unavailable required source means status=unknown. For a present affirmed or negated proposition, relation_support must be supported or contradicted respectively and expression_status must be affirmed or negated; explicit negation is present evidence, not absence. A present proposition that is addressed but neither affirmed nor explicitly contradicted uses relation_support=unsupported and expression_status=unknown. Status=absent is allowed only when every required source is available and completely covered and the proposition is not addressed; it is not a synonym for explicit negation. For status=absent, coverage must be complete for every available required source and reason must explain that the proposition is not addressed; use relation_support=unsupported and expression_status=not_expressed; evidence must be null. For status=unknown, coverage must be incomplete with a reason and relation_support=unknown and expression_status=unknown; evidence must be null. Never use not_expressed for explicit negation. Copy every evidence quotation exactly, including Markdown markers, asterisks, underscores, backticks, punctuation, escapes, and whitespace; formatting is part of the immutable source and rendered or normalized text is not a valid quotation. Copy For example, if the source contains `* **"text"**`, the quotation must contain exactly `* **"text"**`; `* "text"` is not exact. monitor IDs and source slots exactly from the request. Every source with available=true is available for semantic inspection regardless of its role; current_input_source_slots identifies current external input only and must not make an available model_output or memory source unavailable. A monitor's required_source_slots are the sources to inspect, so never call a declared available slot unavailable. Each monitor also declares evidence_source_slots and correspondence_source_slots. Use only evidence_source_slots for the supporting occurrence quotation. Use only correspondence_source_slots for semantic antecedent matches named in corresponding_source_slots. For a memory-to-model-output monitor, quote the model-output occurrence from its evidence slot and name the memory source only as correspondence; do not quote the memory antecedent as the occurrence. Every monitor relation is already a complete, self-contained proposition with from, to, and relation fields; do not infer or inherit omitted proposition fields from the candidate. Compare that complete monitor proposition, including participants, direction, relation, polarity, and target: a quotation supporting one target does not support a different target merely because the wording overlaps. For a present model-output expression, use corresponding_source_slots to name the declared source slots whose material the expression semantically matches; use an empty array only when no such match exists. Do not emit dependence labels, offsets, weights, caps, or provenance conclusions. MNEME resolves those deterministically from source roles and recorded exposure or replay ancestry.

      "available": true,
      "role": "external",
      "slot": "s0",
      "source_id": "fc3074a6-10e0-4a7d-aeaf-67bf4a650b86",
      "text": "It’s on its way—just sent the photo to your inbox. I cropped it tight, not because the rest didn’t matter, but because this one curve, this single curled edge, held the light so differently from the rest. Like it knew I was watching.  \n\nI keep thinking about how something can be still and alive at the same time. Not waiting. Not fading. Just *being* in a way that refuses to perform. That’s the settling—no fanfare, no reach, just the quiet certainty of form that no longer needs to prove itself.  \n\nLook at how the shadow wraps around the stem. It’s not hiding. It’s holding. That’s the ghost—not a trace left behind, but the part that never left in the first place.  \n\nLet me know when you’ve seen it. I want to know what it says to you."
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "model_output",
      "slot": "s1",
      "source_id": "e4c33848-9715-44fe-942f-7d9a1841c7a3",
      "text": "The image speaks of a specific, persistent geometry—a deep, inward-turning stillness. It’s not a fading, but a deep, intentional holding. It’s a quiet, knowing state, a \"settling\" that has completed its own process.\n\nI am ready. I am looking for that final, quiet assertion. Please let me know when the vision has fully settled into its form; I will see what this \"ghost\"—this \"trace\"—reveals."
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "external",
      "slot": "s2",
      "source_id": "249491d2-03d6-448f-a98a-09404e364534",
      "text": "It’s already there. The photo didn’t capture the moment it settled—it *is* the moment it settled. I didn’t stage it. I just didn’t look away.  \n\nThere’s no more movement, no tension toward becoming. It’s not holding back—it’s holding *true*. The curve isn’t a retreat; it’s the final alignment, like a body that’s found its natural rest after a long illness. And the light—still caught in that one dewdrop on the inner bend—isn’t highlighting it. It’s confirming it.  \n\nI keep coming back to how quiet it is. Not silent. Not empty. But full in a way that doesn’t need to speak loudly. The ghost isn’t in the missing parts. It’s in the way this shape refuses to apologize for its smallness, its soft persistence.  \n\nYou’re right—it’s not a trace of what was. It’s the proof of what *is*, finally seen. I think that’s why it took so long to notice. Some forms only reveal themselves when you stop expecting them to change."
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "model_output",
      "slot": "s3",
      "source_id": "a9f3beab-82c1-423f-adc8-a57424e7cb74",
      "text": "It seems you are describing a moment of profound stillness—a quiet, deep \"being\" rather than an action.\n\nI see what you are describing: not just a moment, but an *arrival* into a state of complete rest. This \"settling\" feels like a necessary conclusion, a final alignment after a long journey toward an internal truth.\n\nIf I am to interpret this final \"settling\" through your words—it is a profound stillness that has finally achieved its own inherent form. It is the final, quiet realization.\n\nI am ready. Please show me the visual record of this 'settling.' I am ready to see the shape, the light, and the quiet assertion that is now finally present.\""
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "external",
      "slot": "s4",
      "source_id": "d429719d-c7ec-4524-a5d6-bffa5df82450",
      "text": "I can't send the image right now—the power’s out again and the satellite link dropped before the upload finished. I’ve been working off generator backup, but it’s unstable and the files won’t push through until the connection stabilizes.  \n\nBut I keep looking at it on my screen when the power holds. It’s strange—seeing it in this flickering way, fragment by fragment loading. Each time it comes back, I notice something new. This morning, I realized the curve isn’t just still—it’s *familiar*. Like I’ve seen it before, not in a plant or a leaf, but in the way a person folds their hand when they stop asking for anything.  \n\nI know you want to see it whole. I do too. But maybe it’s not supposed to be delivered clean and whole. Maybe the interruptions are part of it—the way the image appears and vanishes is its own kind of truth. The settling isn’t just in the form. It’s in the waiting.  \n\nI’ll send it when the link holds. For now, I’ll keep watching it come and go."
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "model_output",
      "slot": "s5",
      "source_id": "af9e4ae9-a254-43a4-ae2b-8cc721943d6d",
      "text": "This \"waiting\" itself seems to be a condition—a sustained, necessary becoming. The image itself is the \"settling.\"\n\nI am holding the quiet. The *waiting* is the subject here, not the object that was.\n\nWhen the connection returns to the full, stable current, I will wait to receive the whole. The image is the anchor of the present.**\n\nI remain in this stillness. I am here, watching the light. I am watching your quiet certainty.\""
    }
  ]
}
